hints.title: Candidate Reduction
hints.text: Any element nums[i] can be modified into any value within [nums[i] - k, nums[i] + k]. The optimal target value will always coincide with nums[i], nums[i] - k, or nums[i] + k for some index i.

hints.title: Range Counting
hints.text: Sort nums. For any candidate target v, count how many elements already equal v, and how many elements fall within the reachable range [v - k, v + k].

hints.title: Greedy Operation Allocation
hints.text: The achievable count for target v is the number of exact matches plus min(numOperations, reachable - exact_matches).

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from bisect import bisect_left, bisect_right

class Solution:
    def maxFrequency(self, nums: list[int], k: int, numOperations: int) -> int:
        nums.sort()
        candidates = set()
        for x in nums:
            candidates.add(x)
            candidates.add(x - k)
            candidates.add(x + k)
            
        ans = 0
        for v in candidates:
            left = bisect_left(nums, v - k)
            right = bisect_right(nums, v + k)
            total_in_range = right - left
            exact = bisect_right(nums, v) - bisect_left(nums, v)
            achievable = exact + min(numOperations, total_in_range - exact)
            if achievable > ans:
                ans = achievable
                
        return ans
```

complexity.notes: Sorts nums and checks candidate targets at nums[i], nums[i]-k, and nums[i]+k with binary range queries.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating every possible target value from min to max across huge spans without sorting leads to excessive iterations.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(n) auxiliary space for sorted array queries.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Identifies that optimal target elements must coincide with existing numbers or their interval boundaries.

from bisect import bisect_left, bisect_right

class Solution:
    def maxFrequency(self, nums: list[int], k: int, numOperations: int) -> int:
        nums.sort()
        candidates = set()
        for x in nums:
            candidates.add(x)
            candidates.add(x - k)
            candidates.add(x + k)
            
        ans = 0
        for v in candidates:
            left = bisect_left(nums, v - k)
            right = bisect_right(nums, v + k)
            total_in_range = right - left
            exact = bisect_right(nums, v) - bisect_left(nums, v)
            achievable = exact + min(numOperations, total_in_range - exact)
            if achievable > ans:
                ans = achievable
                
        return ans
